cards.question: What does remotion-maker's pipeline take in, and what does it produce?
cards.answer: A website's brand identity + an operator's script IN; a Remotion video rendered in 30-second chunks OUT.
cards.explanation: The repository holds the reusable workflow (`workflow/`) and the project that instantiates it (`sealcoin-promo/`). The root README is a bare heading: start from `workflow/README.md`. See 02.
cards.anchor: A press takes paint swatches scraped off a shopfront in one hand and a typed script in the other, and extrudes film in reels of equal length.
cards.evidence_quote: into a Remotion video rendered in **30-second chunks**, previewable in a locally hosted Remotion Studio

cards.question: Which timing invariant does remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo fail loudly to protect?
cards.answer: Scene durations must sum to EXACTLY the script's timed map: 4500 frames (75 s at 60 fps).
cards.explanation: Durations are script-true (script seconds x 60) and tile the timeline with no gap. The check runs at module scope, so Studio and every render stop when it fails; see 32.
cards.anchor: A tailor's tape cut to the script's exact length: eight strips of cloth must cover it end to end, no gap and no overhang, or the shop bell rings.
cards.confusables: `TOTAL_FRAMES` — the COMPUTED sum of the scene durations; `EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES` is the DECLARED script total it is checked against.
cards.evidence_quote: export const EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES = 4500; // 75s — synopsis.md §3 map [0-75]

cards.question: In remotion-maker, what is the `sealcoin-promo` directory?
cards.answer: The project that instantiates the workflow: a 75-second explainer for the Eco Wave Power x SEALCOIN x SEALSQ PoC.
cards.explanation: A Remotion 4.0.438 app whose structure was replicated from `h2-promo`. Its script is `sealcoin/synopsis.md` (8 timed segments), its tokens `docs/BRAND.md`, its timing `remotion/manifest.ts`.
cards.confusables: `sealcoin/` (no suffix) — holds ONLY the operator's script `synopsis.md`, read-only ground truth; `sealcoin-promo/` is the app built from it.
cards.evidence_quote: 75-second explainer for the **Eco Wave Power × SEALCOIN × SEALSQ** Autonomous Renewable Energy Marketplace PoC.

cards.question: In remotion-maker, what do the provenance tags `[V]` and `[I]` on a brand token mean?
cards.answer: `[V]` VERIFIED: seen on the live site or stated in the script. `[I]` INFERRED: proposed, needs sign-off.
cards.explanation: Every brand token and every on-screen line carries one; an inferred value is never silently promoted. In sealcoin-promo's `theme.ts` only the orange accent, its gradient stop and two of the three fonts are verified.
cards.example: accentPrimary: "#FF9C1E", // [V] / accentSecondary: "#3EC1F0", // [I]  # same file, different trust
cards.evidence_quote: `[VERIFIED]` (observed on the live site / stated in the operator's script) or `[INFERRED]` (proposed, needs sign-off)

cards.question: remotion-maker: which four fields does one `SceneSpec` entry of sealcoin-promo's `SCENES` hold?
cards.answer: `id`, `label`, `durationInFrames` (script seconds x 60) and `scriptRef` (the script's time range).
cards.explanation: Eight entries in play order: ocean, identity, marketplace, autonomy, trust, scale, pqc, finale. `id` is also the key that picks the scene's React component; `scriptRef` traces the scene to the operator's timed map.
cards.example: { id: "ocean", label: "Ocean energy", durationInFrames: 480, scriptRef: "[0-8s]" }  # 8 s x 60 fps
cards.evidence_quote: { id: "ocean", label: "Ocean energy", durationInFrames: 480, scriptRef: "[0-8s]" },

cards.question: How many frames is one render chunk in remotion-maker, and what running time is that?
cards.answer: 1800 frames = 30 s at 60 fps (`CHUNK_FRAMES`); the last chunk may be partial.
cards.explanation: Chunk count = `ceil(TOTAL_FRAMES / 1800)`. For the 4500-frame sealcoin-promo that is 3 chunks: 1800, 1800 and a partial 900; see 33.
cards.evidence_quote: export const CHUNK_FRAMES = 1800; // 30s @ 60fps

steps: Stage 0 checkpoint -> baseline commit pushed to the remote
Stage 1 brand decomposition: website URL -> `docs/BRAND.md`, 12-section token dictionary
Stage 2 script intake (hard gate): operator script -> `script.md` + `SCENE-MANIFEST.md`
Stage 4 scenes + assets: scene manifest -> scene components and SVG assets

cards.answer: checkpoint · brand decomposition · script gate · scaffold · scenes + assets · chunked render + verify

`npm run concat` -> stream-copies the chunks into `out/sealcoin-promo-75s.mp4`

cards.question: Which command in remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo opens the local preview of the master and every chunk?
cards.answer: `npm run studio` (cwd `sealcoin-promo`) — it runs `remotion studio`.
cards.explanation: Studio lists four compositions, all scrubbable: `SealcoinPromo` plus `SealcoinChunk01/02/03`. Loading them imports the manifest, so this is also where a drift throw first shows; see 32.
cards.confusables: `npm run dev` — starts the inherited Electron shell (`electron-forge start`), whose export button is BROKEN; see 92.

cards.question: remotion-maker · `seriesDuration`: predict the two return values of the calls below. Scene 0 lasts 480 frames, scene 7 (the last of 8) lasts 360, and `TRANSITION_FRAMES` is 12.
cards.answer: `492` and `360` — every scene EXCEPT the last is lengthened by the 12-frame crossfade it hands off into.
cards.explanation: A crossfade overlaps two neighbours, so 7 transitions would eat 84 frames. Derivation: (1) index 0 < 7, so 480 + 12 = 492; (2) index 7 is the last, so 360 + 0; (3) the eight values sum to 4584 and 4584 - 7 x 12 = 4500.
cards.confusables: `sceneStart(index)` — the script-true segment boundary (sum of the durations BEFORE it), with NO crossfade extension.
cards.evidence_quote: (index < SCENES.length - 1 ? TRANSITION_FRAMES : 0);

cards.question: remotion-maker · sealcoin-promo `manifest.ts`: the `ocean` scene is edited from 480 to 500 frames and nothing else changes. Predict the result of starting Studio or any render.
cards.expected_output: Error: Manifest drift: scene durations sum to 4520 frames, expected 4500. Fix SCENES in remotion/manifest.ts (script map: sealcoin/synopsis.md §3).
cards.answer: It THROWS `Manifest drift: scene durations sum to 4520 frames, expected 4500. ...` — the guard sits at module scope, so importing the manifest fails before a single frame is drawn.
cards.explanation: Derivation: 4020 + 500 = 4520, and 4520 !== 4500. The guard protects the script's 75 s map: fix `SCENES`, or, when the script itself changed, change `EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES` too and then see 94.
cards.evidence_quote: `Manifest drift: scene durations sum to ${TOTAL_FRAMES} frames, expected ${EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES}. ` +

cards.question: remotion-maker · `CHUNKS`: predict the four fields of the THIRD element of the array computed below. `TOTAL_FRAMES` is 4500 and `CHUNK_FRAMES` is 1800.
cards.answer: `index 3`, `id "SealcoinChunk03"`, `fromFrame 3600`, `durationInFrames 900` — `ceil(4500 / 1800)` gives 3 windows and the last is PARTIAL (15 s).
cards.explanation: Derivation with i = 2: (1) index 2 + 1 = 3; (2) `padStart(2, "0")` turns 3 into `03`; (3) fromFrame 2 x 1800 = 3600; (4) min(1800, 4500 - 3600) = 900. `Root.tsx` registers one composition per element, passing `fromFrame` as a default prop.
cards.evidence_quote: durationInFrames: Math.min(CHUNK_FRAMES, TOTAL_FRAMES - i * CHUNK_FRAMES),

cards.question: Which is the ONLY file in remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo where a scene's length may be set?
cards.answer: `sealcoin-promo/remotion/manifest.ts` — the `SCENES` array; totals and chunk windows are derived from it.
cards.explanation: `Root.tsx`, the master composition and the chunk wrapper all import their numbers from it. `theme.ts` holds design tokens only; see 61.
cards.confusables: `docs/SCENE-MANIFEST.md` — the human MIRROR of the same table; when the two disagree the code wins and the document is corrected.
cards.evidence_quote: // Scene + chunk manifest — THE single source of truth for all timing.

cards.question: In what order and concurrency does `npm run render:chunks` run remotion-maker's three chunk renders?
cards.answer: One after another: `render:chunk1 && render:chunk2 && render:chunk3` — a failed chunk stops the chain.
cards.explanation: Everything is started by hand on a local machine through npm scripts. The three chunk scripts are HARD-CODED in `package.json`, so a fourth chunk would need a new script; see 94.
cards.evidence_quote: "render:chunks": "npm run render:chunk1 && npm run render:chunk2 && npm run render:chunk3",

cards.question: Which function in remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo makes the background particles identical in every render and every chunk?
cards.answer: `seededRandom(seed)` in `remotion/components/BubbleField.tsx`: the fractional part of `sin(seed * 9301 + 49297) * 233280`, a pure function of the particle index.
cards.explanation: Position, size, speed and delay of each particle come from it. A frame is rendered on its own and a chunk in its own run, so anything random must be reproducible. Breaks if undone: particles differ between runs and jump at a chunk boundary.
cards.confusables: `Math.random()` — a NEW value on every call; `seededRandom(i)` returns the SAME value for the same index forever.
cards.evidence_quote: // Deterministic pseudo-random for consistent renders

cards.question: Why does remotion-maker register each render chunk as `<Sequence from={-fromFrame}>` around the master rather than building each 30 s chunk as its own edit?
cards.answer: A negative `from` slides the ONE master timeline back, so chunk frame 0 shows master frame `fromFrame`: boundaries are pixel-continuous by construction and may fall mid-scene.
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: separately edited chunks must rebuild mid-animation state at every cut by hand, and any retiming moves the cuts. Here chunk 1 ends 2 s into `autonomy` with no special handling. Proof: a still of the master at frame k x 1800 equals a still of chunk k+1 at frame 0.
cards.anchor: One long film strip slides under a fixed half-minute viewing slot. Three cameramen each filming their own half minute would make the wave jump at every handover.
cards.confusables: A separately edited chunk — its frame 0 starts every animation FRESH; a window chunk's frame 0 is the master caught mid-flight.
cards.evidence_quote: master frame `fromFrame`. Boundary continuity is guaranteed by construction.

cards.question: Why does remotion-maker keep scene durations ONLY in `remotion/manifest.ts` rather than also in a `SCENES` table inside `theme.ts`?
cards.answer: Two timing tables drift: in the H2Evo exemplar `theme.SCENES` stopped matching the master composition's real durations. One source plus a module-scope throw makes drift impossible to miss.
cards.explanation: So `theme.ts` holds design tokens only and its `VIDEO` object deliberately has no `durationInFrames`. Breaks if undone: a token table says one length, the render uses another, and nothing fails. See 01 and 32.
cards.anchor: Two clocks in one workshop, one on the paint shelf and one on the bench, slowly disagree and nobody knows which the film obeys. The shelf clock is thrown out; the bench clock gets an alarm.
cards.confusables: `DURATIONS` in `theme.ts` — motion MICRO-timing (fade, pop, stagger, the 12-frame transition), NOT scene lengths.
cards.evidence_quote: its `theme.SCENES` drifted from the master comp's real durations

cards.question: Why does remotion-maker stop at a hard script gate in stage 2 rather than letting the assistant draft scene copy from the brand website?
cards.answer: On-screen copy must be ground truth: final scene copy comes ONLY from the operator's script. Until it arrives, scenes exist only as neutral timing stubs (scene id + frame counter).
cards.explanation: Breaks if undone: invented claims about a partner's product reach a rendered video. Once the script lands and the decomposition is approved, work switches to auto-mode (scenes, assets, chunked render without stops). For sealcoin-promo the script is `sealcoin/synopsis.md`.
cards.anchor: A turnstile that turns only when the operator feeds typed pages into its slot; behind it wait empty boxes, each showing nothing but its name and a running counter.
cards.confusables: Stage 1 brand decomposition — it MAY propose values tagged `[INFERRED]` for sign-off; stage 2 may not start the scene build without the script.
cards.evidence_quote: **No scene visuals or copy may be built from inferred data points.**

cards.question: Why do remotion-maker's chunk render scripts all pass `--muted` rather than letting Remotion embed its default audio track?
cards.answer: Un-muted, each chunk gets a silent AAC track slightly LONGER than its video; the concat demuxer aligns on the longest stream, leaving ~3-frame gaps at every boundary (75.117 s instead of 75.000 s).
cards.explanation: The rule holds only while the composition has no audio. Breaks if undone: the joined file runs long and hitches at each chunk boundary. See 99 for what adding audio would change.
cards.anchor: Three planks, each with a strip of tape glued along it that sticks out a finger past the end: butt them together and the tape holds a crack open at every joint.
cards.confusables: `-c copy` in the concat step — it avoids RE-ENCODING; `--muted` avoids the over-long audio track. The join uses both.
cards.evidence_quote: The concat demuxer aligns segments on the longest stream, so un-muted chunks concat into a video with ~3-frame timestamp gaps at every boundary

cards.question: Where does remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo write its rendered MP4s, and why does the repository contain none?
cards.answer: `sealcoin-promo/out/` — the root `.gitignore` excludes `out/`, so every MP4 must be re-rendered.
cards.explanation: Re-running is safe: `Config.setOverwriteOutput(true)` lets the CLI overwrite and the concat step passes `-y`. The frame-exact results quoted in the runbook therefore cannot be checked from a clone without rendering.
cards.evidence_quote: # Dependencies / build output node_modules/ out/

cards.question: remotion-maker · sealcoin-promo: `out/sealcoin-promo-full.mp4` vs `out/sealcoin-promo-75s.mp4`: what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: `-full` is ONE single-pass render of `SealcoinPromo` (`render:full`, a reference); `-75s` is the CONCATENATION of the chunk files (`concat`), and the only one of the two that `verify:media` checks.
cards.anchor: A loaf baked whole sits on the shelf for comparison; the loaf rebuilt from three slices is the one the inspector measures.
cards.confusables: `out/sealcoin-promo-75s.mp4` — JOINED from chunk files by stream copy; `-full` never passes through the chunk pipeline.
cards.evidence_quote: "render:full": "remotion render SealcoinPromo out/sealcoin-promo-full.mp4 --muted",

cards.question: Where is the `h2-promo` reference implementation that remotion-maker's stage 3 scaffolds from?
cards.answer: NOT in this repository: the root `.gitignore` excludes `h2-promo/` because that folder owns its own nested git repo; the pristine copy lives outside, under `Codebase\h2evo`.
cards.explanation: What survives here of the H2Evo exemplar: the root `workflow.md` (its completed brand dictionary), `Step1.md`-`Step4.md` (its phase prompts), the role prompt `Agents.md` and the tracker `task.md`. On a fresh clone the only app structure left to copy is `sealcoin-promo/`, itself replicated from h2-promo.
cards.evidence_quote: # h2-promo owns its own nested git repo (template lineage, left untouched).

cards.question: What makes remotion-maker's concat and verify scripts able to run ffmpeg and ffprobe on a machine with no system install of them?
cards.answer: They call the binaries BUNDLED with Remotion: `npx remotion ffmpeg` and `npx remotion ffprobe`. Setting env `FFMPEG=ffmpeg` or `FFPROBE=ffprobe` switches to the system binaries.
cards.explanation: Nothing is deployed: preview and renders run locally through npm scripts. The runbook asks to record which binary was used.
cards.example: npm run concat  # spawns: npx remotion ffmpeg -y -f concat ... / set FFMPEG=ffmpeg to spawn the system ffmpeg instead
cards.evidence_quote: // Prefer Remotion's bundled ffmpeg; caller can set FFMPEG=ffmpeg to use system binary.

cards.question: remotion-maker: complete the ffmpeg arguments that `concat-chunks.mjs` uses to join the chunk files.
cards.answer: concat · copy
cards.explanation: The concat DEMUXER reads a list file of `file '<chunk>'` lines discovered from `out/`; `-c copy` stream-copies, so nothing is re-encoded. The join is frame-exact only with muted chunks; see 63.
cards.evidence_quote: args.push("-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", LIST_FILE, "-c", "copy", OUTPUT);

cards.question: Which command proves remotion-maker's sealcoin-promo render is correct, and what is its passing sign?
cards.answer: `npm run verify:media` — it prints `All media checks passed.` after probing each chunk and the concat file.
cards.explanation: It ffprobes the three chunks and the concat file and asserts 30 s / 30 s / 15 s / 75 s within one frame (1/60 s); a missing file counts as a failure and the exit code is 1. Rule: verify by artifacts, not exit codes.
cards.anchor: A customs officer ignores the 'delivered' stamp on the form and puts the parcel itself on the scale.
cards.evidence_quote: console.log("\nAll media checks passed.");

cards.question: remotion-maker · `verify-media.mjs`: ffprobe `stream=duration` vs `format=duration`: what is the ONE difference?
cards.answer: `stream=duration` on `v:0` is FRAME-EXACT (30.000 s for 1800 frames); `format=duration` adds container muxing overhead (chunk 1 read 30.059 s) and would fail the one-frame tolerance.
cards.anchor: Timing a train by the station clock adds the minutes its doors stand open; timing only the wheels turning gives the exact run.
cards.confusables: `format=duration` — the CONTAINER's length including muxing overhead; never assert on it.
cards.evidence_quote: // Video-stream duration, not format duration: the mp4 container reports a few

cards.question: remotion-maker: you start sealcoin-promo's Electron UI with `npm run dev` and click its render button. What happens, and how do you render instead?
cards.answer: The render fails: `src/render-video.ts` hard-codes `compositionId = "HelloWorld"`, an id `Root.tsx` does NOT register. Render through the CLI scripts (`npm run render:chunks`).
cards.explanation: The Electron `src/` tree is inherited from the template and kept only for structure parity; `remotion/types.ts` still holds only `HelloWorldProps`. The registered ids are `SealcoinPromo` and `SealcoinChunk01/02/03`.
cards.evidence_quote: const compositionId = "HelloWorld";

cards.question: remotion-maker: following the vendored `remotion-best-practices` rules you add `premountFor` to a `<Sequence>` in sealcoin-promo and type-checking fails. Which rule settles it, and what do you do?
cards.answer: The PINNED version wins: Remotion is fixed at 4.0.438, where `Sequence premountFor` does not exist. Strip the prop (the H2Evo build stripped 10 usages) and re-run `npm run lint`.
cards.explanation: The rules under `.agents/skills/remotion-best-practices/` are third-party and describe newer APIs; `skills-lock.json` pins them by hash. `npm run lint` ends with `tsc --noEmit`, which is what catches the missing prop before a render.
cards.evidence_quote: When a rule and the pinned version disagree, the pinned version wins.

cards.question: remotion-maker: the script grows to 100 s (6000 frames). sealcoin-promo's README says retiming only ever means editing scene durations in `manifest.ts`. Which other places must change, and what goes wrong at each if it does not?
cards.answer: Three more places; the one-file claim is DRIFT. (1) `EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES` in `manifest.ts`: left at 4500, the drift guard throws on import. (2) `scripts/verify-media.mjs` repeats `CHUNK_FRAMES` and `EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES`: it still expects 3 chunks and 75 s. (3) `package.json` has only `render:chunk1..3`: `ceil(6000 / 1800)` = 4, so `SealcoinChunk04` is registered but never rendered.
cards.explanation: The output name `sealcoin-promo-75s.mp4` is also hard-coded in both scripts. Only a `keep in sync` comment guards the duplicated constants. The concat step is the one part that adapts by itself: it discovers chunk files from `out/`.
cards.evidence_quote: const EXPECTED_TOTAL_FRAMES = 4500; // keep in sync with remotion/manifest.ts

cards.question: remotion-maker · resume: sealcoin-promo was rendered as a video-only pass, with the script's voice-over kept as metadata. When audio is added, which parts of the chunk pipeline stop being valid?
cards.answer: The `--muted` + stream-copy join. (1) Every render script passes `--muted`, a rule stated only for compositions WITHOUT audio. (2) Un-muted chunks carry an AAC track slightly longer than their video, so the concat demuxer leaves ~3-frame gaps at each boundary. (3) `verify-media.mjs` probes only the video stream `v:0`, so it cannot see audio drift.
cards.explanation: DESIGN TARGET: no audio code exists, and the repository names no next step for sealcoin-promo in so many words (root `task.md` lists voiceover integration as future work, but for the H2Evo exemplar); audio is the open item its documents point at. Whatever replaces the join must be proved the same way: by probing the produced file.
cards.evidence_quote: All voice-over text is production metadata only (no audio in this pass)
